perspective:
**From Arthur Chung’s perspective:**

I know I am Arthur Chung, a highly educated plumber. I know Teresa Ortega as a medical assistant colleague; we’ve worked together on community service projects, generally respect each other, share a commitment to helping others, and sometimes misunderstand each other.

During this project:
- I noticed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. I felt concerned and believed she needed help, so I offered assistance.
- Teresa said she thought she could manage but had a lot to do. After I insisted, she accepted help organizing medical supplies. We started.
- I believed she was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. I felt empathy and tried to reassure her that accepting help doesn’t mean she’s incapable. Teresa said she appreciated it, wanted to show she could do it herself, and later agreed she sometimes needs reminding. I said teamwork is more effective and that I support her.
- I believed she was still struggling and felt frustrated that my help wasn’t yielding results. I wanted to support her without making her feel inadequate. Teresa said it had been busy and she felt behind. I proposed working together instead of just helping her; she agreed.
- I believed collaboration would ease her burden and improve efficiency. I felt hopeful and committed. Teresa agreed it felt less overwhelming. I suggested I handle inventory while she managed patient records and we check in regularly; she agreed.
- Afterward, I believed our teamwork paid off and strengthened our professional relationship. I felt satisfied. Teresa agreed it was a great experience and that we were more efficient/effective as a team. I suggested continuing collaboration on future projects; she agreed and thanked me for being supportive.
